إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ
فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ذَنُوبًا مِّثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَٰبِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن يَوْمِهِمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ

Only in Ea's proposal: a god is slain and man made from his flesh, blood and clay (Atra-hasis OB I 174-239): A burden that higher beings refuse or throw off is laid on, or taken up by, humankind [divergence between the texts]; One god, the ringleader 'who had the plan', is slaughtered in the assembly so that humankind can be made; The great gods spit upon the clay from which humankind is to be formed; From the slain god's flesh a ghost (eṭemmu) remains in humans, and a heartbeat (drum) is heard in them forever, so that he is not forgotten; Humankind is made of clay mixed with the flesh and blood of a slaughtered god, so that god and man are mixed together; A purification bath is instituted on the first, seventh and fifteenth days of the month; The creator declares 'I am the one who created, my hands have made it'; The divine beings ask for, or object to, the making of humans [divergence between the texts]; What divine element is put into the clay of the first human: a slain god's flesh, blood and spirit, or God's breath [divergence between the texts]; A god fashions a creature from clay to serve his purpose; Humankind is created as a substitute to take over the gods' toil and carry their work-basket; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship: Of everything God created pairs (zawjayn); 'So flee to God; I am to you a clear warner from him'; God created jinn and humans only to worship him; he wants no provision or food from them; The wrongdoers have a portion (dhanub, a bucketful) of punishment like that of their fellows; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; Whether God, or the gods, eat the offerings [contrast between the texts]; What God created humans, or his people, for [divergence between the texts]; God built the sky with might (bi-aydin) and is expanding it (inna la-musi'un); The deity declines the mortal's gifts of food or offerings [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; No messenger came to earlier peoples without being called 'a sorcerer or a madman', as if they had bequeathed the charge to one another; Whether the deity is hungry and thirsty and is fed by worshippers [response between the texts]; and 2 more.

matches.label: How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response
matches.note: How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and what follows. Genesis: YHWH decides ha-mḵasseh ʾănî mē-ʾaḇrāhām and tells him of the outcry (zaʿăqaṯ səḏōm), and Abraham bargains for the city (18:23-32). matches.label: Who Abraham's visitors are
matches.note: Who the visitors are. Genesis: wa-yērāʾ ʾēlâw YHWH bə-ʾēlōnê mamrēʾ ... wə-hinnēh šəlōšâ ʾănāšîm (YHWH appears, as three men; YHWH himself speaks in 18:13). Quran: ḍayfu ibrāhīma l-mukramīn, addressed as ayyuhā l-mursalūn (51:31): honored guests who are 'sent ones', no number, and God is not among them.

passages.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵלֹנֵ֖י מַמְרֵ֑א וְה֛וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב פֶּֽתַח הָאֹ֖הֶל כְּחֹ֥ם הַיּֽוֹם
וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

matches.label: Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them
matches.note: The welcome. Genesis: Abraham runs to meet them (wa-yyāroṣ liqrāʾṯām), bows to the ground and begs ʾăḏōnāy ʾim nāʾ māṣāʾṯî ḥēn bə-ʿênêḵā, then wa-yəmahēr ʾaḇrāhām hā-ʾōhĕlâ ʾel śārâ. Quran: the guests speak first, fa-qālū salāman qāla salāmun qawmun munkarūn (Abraham returns the greeting and finds them strange), then fa-rāgha ilā ahlihi (he slipped off to his household). Same hurried move to the tent; the bow and the plea are absent, and Abraham's unease (munkarūn) is added.

passages.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֗י אִם נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אַל נָ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר מֵעַ֥ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ
וַיְמַהֵ֧ר אַבְרָהָ֛ם הָאֹ֖הֱלָה אֶל שָׂרָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַהֲרִ֞י שְׁלֹ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קֶ֣מַח סֹ֔לֶת ל֖וּשִׁי וַעֲשִׂ֥י עֻגֽוֹת
إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ

matches.label: Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal
matches.note: Reversal: in Genesis the visitors eat: wə-hûʾ ʿōmēḏ ʿălêhem taḥaṯ hā-ʿēṣ wa-yyōʾḵēlû. In the Quran they do not: qāla a-lā taʾkulūn, fa-awjasa minhum khīfatan, qālū lā takhaf. The refusal to eat reveals that they are angels and frightens Abraham. cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14 and b. Bava Metzia 86b (the angels only seemed to eat), a solution to the same problem; not in the HB.

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ

matches.label: Sarah's reaction to the announcement of a son
matches.note: Sarah's reaction, changed from inner laughter to an open cry. Genesis: wat-tiṣḥaq śārâ bə-qirbāh lēʾmōr ʾaḥărê ḇəlōṯî ... wa-ʾḏōnî zāqēn; God asks lāmmâ zeh ṣāḥăqâ śārâ and she denies it out of fear (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾâ). Quran: fa-aqbalati mraʾatuhu fī ṣarratin fa-ṣakkat wajhahā wa-qālat ʿajūzun ʿaqīm (she came forward crying out, struck her face and said 'a barren old woman!'). The messengers answer ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm: no rebuke, no denial, no laughter (ṣ-ḥ-q, the pun on Isaac's name, is gone).

passages.text: וַתִּצְחַ֥ק שָׂרָ֖ה בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַחֲרֵ֤י בְלֹתִי֙ הָֽיְתָה לִּ֣י עֶדְנָ֔ה וַֽאדֹנִ֖י זָקֵֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל אַבְרָהָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּה֩ צָחֲקָ֨ה שָׂרָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הַאַ֥ף אֻמְנָ֛ם אֵלֵ֖ד וַאֲנִ֥י זָקַֽנְתִּי
וַתְּכַחֵ֨שׁ שָׂרָ֧ה לֵאמֹ֛ר לֹ֥א צָחַ֖קְתִּי כִּ֣י יָרֵ֑אָה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לֹ֖א כִּ֥י צָחָֽקְתְּ
فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

matches.label: The answer given to the old woman's doubt
matches.note: The answer to the old woman's doubt: hă-yippālēʾ mē-YHWH dāḇār (is anything too wondrous for YHWH?, a rhetorical question by YHWH himself) vs. ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm (thus said your Lord; he is the Wise, the Knowing, said by the messengers). Divine power becomes divine wisdom and knowledge, and the speaker is the angels quoting God.

passages.text: הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן
قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

matches.label: A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests
matches.note: wa-yiqqaḥ ben bāqār raḵ wā-ṭôḇ ... wa-yiqqaḥ ḥemʾâ wə-ḥālāḇ û-ḇen hab-bāqār ... wa-yittēn lip̄nêhem vs. fa-jāʾa bi-ʿijlin samīnin fa-qarrabahu ilayhim. Genesis: a tender, good calf with curds and milk; Quran: a fat calf only.

passages.text: וְאֶל הַבָּקָ֖ר רָ֣ץ אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֶּן בָּקָ֜ר רַ֤ךְ וָטוֹב֙ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל הַנַּ֔עַר וַיְמַהֵ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֹתֽוֹ
וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

matches.label: A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name
matches.note: wə-hinnēh ḇēn lə-śārâ ʾištekā; lam-môʿēḏ ʾāšûḇ ʾēleḵā kā-ʿēṯ ḥayyâ û-lə-śārâ ḇēn vs. wa-bashsharūhu bi-ghulāmin ʿalīm. Genesis promises a son to Sarah with a set time; the Quran gives the good news to Abraham of 'a knowing boy', with no time and no name.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה וְהִנֵּה בֵ֖ן לְשָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו
הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן

فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ

leads.title: I have called you by name; you are my witnesses; behold I do a new thing ↔ The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: What God created humans, or his people, for [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in I have called you by name; you are my witnesses; behold I do a new thing: 'Your first father sinned and your interpreters (melitsim) transgressed against me'; God says to north 'Give up' and to south 'Do not withhold': bring my sons from afar and my daughters from the end of the earth; The wild beasts, jackals and ostriches honor God for the water he gives in the desert; God gives Egypt, Cush and Seba as Israel's ransom (kofer) and peoples in exchange for her life; 'I, I am YHWH, and besides me there is no savior'; 'Do not remember the former things... Behold I am doing a new thing; now it springs forth': a way in the wilderness, rivers in the desert; Israel did not weary itself with offerings for God but wearied him with its sins; he blots out transgressions for his own sake; 'Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine'; Every one of you will come to (pass by) hell; then the pious are rescued; Cry 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon!' and all her idols shattered on the ground; God himself devotes the nations (or a nation) to destruction (herem) and gives them to slaughter; Those with knowledge of the earlier Book are invoked as witnesses to the prophet's mission [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship: Of everything God created pairs (zawjayn); 'So flee to God; I am to you a clear warner from him'; God created jinn and humans only to worship him; he wants no provision or food from them; The wrongdoers have a portion (dhanub, a bucketful) of punishment like that of their fellows; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; Whether God, or the gods, eat the offerings [contrast between the texts]; God built the sky with might (bi-aydin) and is expanding it (inna la-musi'un); The deity declines the mortal's gifts of food or offerings [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; No messenger came to earlier peoples without being called 'a sorcerer or a madman', as if they had bequeathed the charge to one another; Whether the deity is hungry and thirsty and is fed by worshippers [response between the texts]; God does not need sacrifices: 'If I were hungry I would not tell you... Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?'; and 2 more.

Only in Psalm 50 - God summons heaven and earth; do I eat the flesh of bulls: Superscription ascribes the psalm to Asaph; Every beast of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills, and the ziz of the field; God's faithful ones made a covenant with him by sacrifice; Our God comes and is not silent; fire devours before him and a tempest rages around him; Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth (hofia); 'I kept silent, and you thought I was one like yourself'; An oath invoking God by a repeated triple title (El, Elohim, YHWH); Whether God is in need and humans rich [contrast between the texts]; Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving (todah) and pay your vows to Elyon; God rebukes the wicked who recites his statutes and covenant yet consorts with thieves and adulterers; Poet summons heaven and earth to listen; Wonder done 'so that you may know that the earth belongs to YHWH'; and 4 more.

Only in The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship: Of everything God created pairs (zawjayn); 'So flee to God; I am to you a clear warner from him'; God created jinn and humans only to worship him; he wants no provision or food from them; The wrongdoers have a portion (dhanub, a bucketful) of punishment like that of their fellows; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; Whether God, or the gods, eat the offerings [contrast between the texts]; What God created humans, or his people, for [divergence between the texts]; God built the sky with might (bi-aydin) and is expanding it (inna la-musi'un); The deity declines the mortal's gifts of food or offerings [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; No messenger came to earlier peoples without being called 'a sorcerer or a madman', as if they had bequeathed the charge to one another; Whether the deity is hungry and thirsty and is fed by worshippers [response between the texts]; and 2 more.

matches.note: God needs no food from his worshippers: ʾim ʾerʿaḇ lōʾ ʾōmar lāḵ ... ha-ʾôḵal bəśar ʾabbîrîm wə-ḏam ʿattûḏîm ʾeštê vs. mā urīdu minhum min rizqin wa-mā urīdu an yuṭʿimūn, inna llāha huwa r-razzāq. The psalm argues against sacrifice as feeding God, then asks for thanksgiving (zəḇaḥ tôḏâ, 50:14); the Quran makes God the provider (razzāq) and worship ('ibāda) the purpose of creation.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The old wife overhears the promise of a son at the tent door and laughs (weight 7.3); A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests (weight 7.3); A guest refuses to sit on the chair offered, to touch the table or to put his lip to the cup (weight 7.3); Abraham's angelic guests do not stretch their hands to the food, and he is afraid (weight 7.3); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.8). Pair score 35.2.

Only in Abraham's guests, the roasted calf and the laughing wife: Abraham is forbearing, sighing (awwah) and penitent; The annunciation names Isaac 'and after Isaac, Jacob'; Promised son born to aged parents at the appointed time; Whether the divine guest eats the meal prepared by the host [divergence between the texts]; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age; Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why [divergence between the texts]; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response; Who Abraham's visitors are; A host sets meat before an arriving messenger, who does not take the meal, and fear follows [divergence between the texts]; How God answers Abraham's plea for the people of Sodom [divergence between the texts]; An intercessor pleads with the divine to spare a city whose destruction is decreed; the decree is not turned back [divergence between the texts]; When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered; and 9 more.

Only in Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah: On 'Ad God sent the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim), which left everything like rotten bones; Abraham brings a fattened calf but the guests do not eat, and he becomes afraid of them; The honored guests enter saying 'Peace' and Abraham replies 'Peace, strangers (qawm munkarun)'; The guests announce to Abraham a knowing (or wise) son ('alim); Thamud were told 'Enjoy yourselves for a while', defied the command and were seized by the thunderbolt while they looked on; Abraham's wife comes forward crying out, strikes her face and says 'A barren old woman!'; Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Supernatural envoys who come to seize or destroy do not eat the food offered them [divergence between the texts]; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; The host, seeing the divine visitor, has his household prepare an animal from the herd (lamb, calf) for the guest; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

leads.title: al-yamm: the sea word reserved for Moses
leads.summary: The Quran's usual word for sea is bahr, but al-yamm appears 8 times across 4 surahs, always in the Moses/Pharaoh narrative. It is the Semitic sea word shared with Hebrew yam, Ugaritic Yam, and Mandaic yama, and borrowed into New Kingdom Egyptian.
